DEC-004.title: Accept per-process in-memory caches under multi-worker staleness
DEC-004.rationale: Post list (TTL 300s) and categories/tags (TTL 1800s) caches are process-local TTLCache. docker-compose runs uvicorn --workers 2, so each worker invalidates only its own cache on writes; the other worker serves stale entries bounded by TTL (≤5min posts, ≤30min taxonomies). At this blog's scale the worst-case staleness is cosmetic and self-heals; views/likes never invalidate list cache by design (ordering unchanged).
DEC-004.alternatives_rejected: Redis-backed shared cache (new infra + ops cost, no multi-node deployment yet); single uvicorn worker (loses concurrency for a latent-cosmetic gain); versioned cache keys with a shared clock (still needs Redis to be correct).

Scope: extract a reusable conditional-response helper (strong ETag from body + If-None-Match 304 + Cache-Control) from _feed_response; apply to all cacheable public GETs with per-resource revalidation windows (public, max-age ~ TTL-based); set no-store on write-on-read/post-detail and leave private admin/search uncached; contract tests (200 then 304, ETag stability across cache hits, Cache-Control per endpoint class); e2e journey through the Nuxt proxy verifying 200->304 conditional workflow; document the cache policy. (c) Debounce view/like write-on-read (TASK-026) — independent perf item, keep tracked; this milestone instead makes the detail/views path explicitly no-store, which bounds the correctness side of the same concern without the write-queue redesign. DEC-088.title: Milestone: sanitized Markdown rendering in comments
DEC-088.rationale: Feature-evolution selection (SKILL 11.2 gap analysis). A tech blog lives on code discussion, but comments render as plain pre-wrap text: a fenced code block or inline `code`/emphasis shows its raw markdown, hurting readability exactly where readers share snippets. Milestone: render comment content through the SAME sanitized markdown pipeline as post content (marked with breaks:true to keep single newlines, then sanitizeHtml — DOMPurify when loaded, always-on regex fallback otherwise), so code blocks/emphasis render and a <script> in a comment still never executes; add a "supports Markdown" hint to the comment form. Frontend-only (comment storage stays raw; the RSS/export/backup paths already carry the raw text). Tests: CommentList component (markdown rendering + XSS strip) + E2E posting a code/script comment.
DEC-088.alternatives_rejected: Reader notification-center: redundant with account.vue (devices/want_new_posts/followed category/threads already managed there). Email digests: no SMTP infra. Comment editing/deleting by author: larger auth surface (comment ownership), separate slice. Syntax highlighting in comments: enhancement after baseline markdown rendering. Math/mermaid in comments: out of scope (posts-only).

DEC-090.title: Milestone: syntax highlighting in comment code blocks
DEC-090.rationale: Feature-evolution selection (SKILL 11.2 gap analysis): DEC-088 delivered sanitized markdown rendering in comments but explicitly deferred syntax highlighting as an enhancement after the baseline. Now that fences render, a tech blog discussion still falls flat — a ts snippet in a comment is monochrome while the identical snippet in the post body is Tokyo Night highlighted. Users: readers posting/sharing snippets in discussion threads. Why now: the render pipeline exists and useCodeHighlight already ships for posts (lazy client-only highlight.js + escapeHtml fallback), so the slice is a frontend-only augment with no schema change. Acceptance (one sentence): an approved comment fenced code block shows highlight.js token colors reusing the post Tokyo Night theme. Scope: lazily load loadHighlighter in CommentList, tokenize each .comment-body pre code on mount, apply shared token CSS, fall back to plain escaped text; keep existing XSS guarantees (highlightCode escapes its source).

TASK-158.title: Comment likes/upvotes: comments.likes column + POST /comments/{id}/like + per-comment like button with localStorage dedup + tests

DEC-092.title: Milestone: comment likes (upvotes)
DEC-092.rationale: Feature-evolution selection (SKILL 11.2 gap analysis): with comments now rendering markdown and highlighted code, discussion threads still lack a lightweight community signal — readers share code, but there is no way to signal "this snippet/answer helped me" without writing another comment. Post likes (POST /posts/{id}/like, anonymous count++) already set the precedent; extending the same pattern to comments is a natural vertical slice on the comments arc (DEC-088 markdown -> DEC-090 highlight -> likes). Users: readers evaluating whether past questions were answered; authors scanning which comments helped. Acceptance (one sentence): a reader can like (and dedup-prevent re-like of) a comment, and the count is visible on every published comment. Scope: additive comments.likes column + POST /comments/{id}/like (rate-limited, 404 for comments on non-public posts) + CommentPublic.likes; per-comment like button in CommentList (heart + count, localStorage dedup like the post-like ISS-038 pattern, optimistic update, error handling) + en/zh labels; backend pytest + frontend component + E2E.
DEC-092.alternatives_rejected: Comment code copy button (tiny, frontend-only, could fold into a later slice); comment editing/deleting by author (larger auth/ownership surface, separate slice); comment dislikes (negative engagement, out); per-reader like identity (would need a new table + JWT wiring — anonymous count matches the post-likes precedent).

Frontend: useCommentLike + Comment.likes in useApi; CommentList renders a per-comment heart+count button (top-level and replies) with optimistic update from the response, a localStorage liked-comments:<id> guard (one like per browser, mirroring the post-like ISS-038 pattern), in-flight spinner, and localized error. Tests: backend comment suite (increment per request, exposed on public approved list, 404 unknown, 404 on non-public post) + full suite green (93.91% cov); frontend vitest 1017 (like click updates count + marks localStorage, dedup no-op, error path); biome + vue-tsc + pyright clean; Playwright comment-likes (count 0->1, aria-pressed, second click deduped) + comment-markdown regression green.
DEC-093.alternatives_rejected: Comment code copy button (deferred to a later slice); comment editing/deleting by author (auth/ownership surface, separate slice); per-reader like identity (needs a new table + JWT wiring, anonymous count matches post-likes); comment dislikes (negative engagement, out).

DEC-094.title: Milestone: comment sorting by likes (most helpful)
DEC-094.rationale: Feature-evolution selection (SKILL 11.2 gap analysis) on the comments arc. DEC-092 shipped a per-comment likes counter, but the public comment list still renders strictly newest-first (crud.get_comments_paginated orders by created_at desc), so likes carry no ordering value — on a long thread readers share snippets and answers with no way to surface which comments helped. Milestone: let readers sort the approved comment list by Most helpful (likes desc), Newest, or Oldest. Users: readers landing on a long thread who want the best/answered question first; authors scanning which comments helped. Why now: the likes column already exists (DEC-092/TASK-158), so this is a pure additive slice with no schema change — it activates the likes data into a user-facing ordering dimension. Acceptance (one sentence): a reader can switch the thread to Most helpful/Newest/Oldest and the approved comment list reorders accordingly. Scope: add a whitelisted sort param (newest default | oldest | likes) to GET /api/comments/post/{id} and crud.get_comments_paginated (likes desc, created_at desc tiebreak), a sort toggle in CommentList (re-fetch with selected sort), i18n labels (en/zh), frontend component + backend pytest + E2E.
DEC-094.alternatives_rejected: Comment code copy button (tiny, frontend-only, low value-gate — "missing a button" level, rejected per SKILL 11.2); comment editing/deleting by author (larger auth/ownership surface, keep as a separate slice); comment dislikes (negative engagement, out); comment collapsing/summarizing by likes (scope creep, threads are flat already).

DEC-096.title: Milestone: comment editing/deleting by author (reader-owned comments)
DEC-096.rationale: Feature-evolution selection (SKILL 11.2 gap analysis) on the comments arc. The comments arc has matured (DEL-088 markdown -> DEC-090 highlight -> DEC-092 likes -> DEC-094 sorting) but a signed-in reader has no way to correct or retract their own comment: a typo or misstatement is permanent unless a moderator deletes it. Readers who authenticate (reader accounts, DEC-059/062) chat and share code under a verified identity, so ownership is knowable. Milestone: let a reader edit or delete their own reader-attributed comments. Users: signed-in readers who want to fix a typo or withdraw something they posted; moderators who no longer have to delete trivial self-corrections. Why now: reader accounts already attach reader_id to comments, so ownership auth is a clean additive slice on the existing comments surface (no schema change beyond an optional edited_at/edit history flag). Acceptance (one sentence): a signed-in reader can edit the text of their own comment and delete their own comment, and neither action affects other comments or anonymous ones. Scope: backend PATCH/DELETE /api/comments/{id} guarded by ownership (reader_id == current reader; 404/403 without leaking ownership; PATCH preserves post_id/parent_id, re-sanitizes content server-side, bumps optional edited_at, re-renders via the existing markdown/highlight pipeline); DELETE removes the comment and reparents/removes its replies consistently; frontend Edit/Delete controls rendered only on the reader is own comments, inline edit form reusing CommentForm, confirm-on-delete, localized labels; backend pytest (ownership, 404/403, anonymous/reader, reply handling) + frontend component + E2E.
DEC-096.alternatives_rejected: Comment code copy button (tiny, frontend-only, low value-gate, kept as a possible later slice); comment editing/deleting of ANY comment by moderators (admin already deletes via existing endpoint); comment dislikes (negative engagement, out); editing anonymous comments (no owner identity, out); soft-delete/tombstone toggle (bigger surface, not needed yet).
